stories.name: Meta enterprise AI push
stories.blurb: Meta is making a major push into enterprise AI, hiring MongoDB CEO CJ Desai to lead a new enterprise platform unit and pitching businesses on running on its AI stack.

stories.name: Meta Muse AI agent
stories.blurb: Meta's new Muse AI agent has sparked a sharp rally in Meta stock as investors and analysts bet it could become a major competitive threat to Google and a landmark AI product.

stories.name: Meta Stock Debate
stories.blurb: Investors and analysts weigh in on Meta Platforms' stock valuation and buying opportunities following Q2 2026 earnings, AI spending returns, and a recent price selloff.

stories.name: Meta's AI data center buildout
stories.blurb: Meta is spending tens of billions of dollars building massive AI data centers across the U.S. and Canada, often through joint ventures like its partnership with BlackRock.

stories.name: Meta Child Addiction Lawsuits
stories.blurb: State and individual lawsuits accuse Meta of deliberately designing Facebook and Instagram to be addictive to children, leading to court rulings, trials, and multibillion-dollar settlements/penalties

stories.name: AI Stock Rally
stories.blurb: A broad rally in AI-related stocks, including Meta, AMD, and semiconductor companies, is driving major market gains and record highs amid growing enthusiasm for artificial intelligence technology.

rel.why: Meta's Muse AI agent is driving the AI stock rally and AMD's $1T milestone, directly reflecting Meta's product success and market impact.

stories.name: AI safety and regulation
stories.blurb: Tech companies and governments are grappling with how to regulate and ensure the safety of increasingly powerful AI models amid rapid releases and high-profile incidents.

stories.name: Meta AI turnaround
stories.blurb: Meta's stock is surging as the company transforms from an AI laggard into a leader, with its AI push reshaping advertising, wearables, and data center plans.

past.name: Meta AI cloud business
past.blurb: Meta is reportedly building a cloud computing business to sell its excess AI compute capacity, positioning itself as a rival to AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud.

past.name: Digital Ad Stock Watch
past.blurb: Coverage of how Meta's social-media and ad-tech peers—Pinterest, Snap, Reddit, and AppLovin—are performing in the market amid shifts in advertising demand and user growth.

past.name: Meta Power Deals
past.blurb: Meta's contracts with energy companies like Vistra and Cogentrix to secure electricity for its data centers are fueling investor interest in power and nuclear-related stocks.

past.name: Meta's Muse AI Agent
past.blurb: Meta launched Muse, its first personal AI agent and coding assistant, as part of a broader push into AI to compete with OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google while facing scrutiny over privacy and safety.

13.text: Meta is co-building standards for business interactions with AI bots and launched a free AI agent that hit 5 million downloads. It also parted ways with Virtue AI hires, Zuckerberg sold $21.3 million in stock, and Mark Cuban accused Facebook of running deepfake scam ads.

14.text: Meta launched its Muse personal AI agent on September 8, which hit 5 million downloads and topped app charts, with partnerships including Walmart, Gap, and Best Buy. Analysts estimate Muse could generate $27 billion annually by 2030, though Amazon blocked it from its platform.

8.text: Meta’s ad business is strong, with shares up about 19–22% recently, but analysts debate whether AI and capex spending, plus a rich valuation, justify further gains. Wells Fargo set a $1,000 target while warning of a rough year, and Meta fell 2.38% on Oct 7.

6.text: Hyperscalers are increasingly funding AI infrastructure with debt as free cash flow turns negative and costs rise, with Alphabet spending more on AI than its cash flow. Analysts warn this borrowing binge and chip commoditization could strain markets, though Meta is barely mentioned.

9.text: Meta’s AI data center expansion is driving federal support for new nuclear power and renewable energy projects, plus over 20 subsea cable investments for data capacity. Meta’s tax credits also jumped from about $700 million to $3.9 billion, drawing accusations it uses AI data centers to avoid federal taxes.

7.text: New Mexico is seeking up to $40 billion from Meta after a jury found it misled users on privacy, with a ruling due this month. Florida rejected an $18 billion settlement and wants a court to disable infinite scroll for teens, while UK regulator Ofcom opened a probe into Instagram Instants' child safety risks.

11.text: Meta's Muse AI agent runs on AMD EPYC processors, and Morgan Stanley estimates it could drive 20% of AMD's 2026 chip sales. This demand helped push AMD stock to record highs and a $1 trillion market cap.

16.text: Meta joined five other AI companies in signing a voluntary White House pact accepting outside audits of its safety controls, which Trump called "morally binding." Other articles cover OpenAI, Anthropic, and a new federal "Super Intelligence" task force, barely touching Meta.

17.text: Meta’s AI spending is boosting Micron’s profits and operating income, with Micron’s stronger finances potentially enabling stock buybacks. Other articles mainly cover Nvidia, AMD, Nike, and SpaceX, barely bearing on Meta beyond a former CTO interview.
